answer: Each agent identity is bound to one scarce ferrous assay slug whose grain pattern cannot be copied in software. At registration the registrar photographs that grain beside an embedded opal serial chip, hashes both, and later issues a pulsed-field challenge only that physical slug can echo. Anyone who wants another seat must buy a second slug from the capped mint and present it in person at a remote dune assay post for the same check, so each fake ID costs another limited slug plus travel and time rather than a cheap scripted clone.
